ns2:section.sectionText: Conservation policy evaluation is a rapidly growing field of inquiry that is transforming our understanding of what works, what does not, and why in biodiversity conservation. This course will examine how new developments (big data, remote sensing data, machine learning) in combination with robust evaluation methods can help answer the central evaluation question: did the conservation intervention make a difference compared to no intervention at all? Rigorous answers to this question is critical to strengthen the evidence base to inform the design of more effective conservation interventions. The course should be of special interest to graduate students (in NRES, ACE, Geography, Political Science, and other programs) interested to learn about current methods to assess conservation and other environmental policies.
